evidence: The claim 'releases only through v4' is refuted inside the packet itself: rounds 1-3 of this very review were produced by the workflow that checks out with actions/checkout@v6, so the step resolved. Flag is a false positive: 327c152 only touched test/default-dsl-config.test.ts; the workflow line was in the PR from the start.

Same stale-knowledge claim as F1, and the workflow demonstrably ran on this PR. The pushback is right, but [LAW:single-enforcer] is about enforcing an invariant in one place; 'the install template owns this generated file' is a one-source-of-truth/generated-output argument. Flag false positive: 8fb6e51 is a master merge (CHANGELOG, candybar-lite, versions) that did not touch the workflow.

validateConfig(merged, "<merged>", SERIALIZED) passes the bundled default's text as the source that errors quote, while validating a different object; 8c7e0b3 passes JSON.stringify(merged, null, 2). The SERIALIZED arg was in the original helper, not added by 327c152, so the post-review flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When copying a sibling test helper, re-derive every argument for the new input; a 'source' parameter carried over from the default-config helper no longer matches what is validated.

evidence: A third copy of the checkout@v6 claim in the same round; the workflow ran on this PR, so v6 resolves. The law token is pasted onto a 'template owns this file' argument, as in F2. The flag is a false positive because 8fb6e51 did not touch the workflow.
This repeats F1. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 8c7e0b3 only changed the validateConfig source argument in the test file, and the workflow line is unchanged from the original PR.
This duplicates F5 in the same round. The workflow ran with @v6, which refutes the claim. Flag false positive: 8c7e0b3 did not touch .github/workflows/code-review.yml.

The finding is a hedge ('if the repository does not exist...'). The packet answers it: rounds 1-3 are signed 'Reviewed by config auto→deepseek', which means brandon-fryslie/coding-agent-review@v1 ran with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. Flag false positive: 8c7e0b3 was a test-only change.

narrative: The only real code finding was F3, a mis-sourced validateConfig argument in the test helper, and it was fixed cleanly. The other six findings are one stale-model claim (actions/checkout@v6 'does not exist') plus a hedge about the renamed action, re-raised across three rounds. The PR's own review runs disprove both. None of the later rounds was caused by a fix; they were triggered by the reviewer repeating a false claim and by a master merge (8fb6e51).
guidance_observations: The agent pushed back correctly, but each pushback rested on an off-packet API check; pointing to the in-PR evidence that the workflow had just executed would have been a self-contained proof.
Pasting [LAW:single-enforcer] onto a 'generated file owned by a template' argument dilutes the token; the argument stood without it.

evidence: readPayload returns JSON.parse(raw) unvalidated, so a stdin of `null` makes `data.workspace?.current_dir` throw TypeError on `null.workspace` (`?.` only guards the property). render's `data.context_window` was equally exposed in the original, so the gap predates the round-0/1 fixes, and fb47ba3 (the 100% cap) is unrelated. The PR merged with this thread unanswered and unresolved.
guidance_note: When hardening a parse boundary for 'malformed input', validate the parsed shape (a plain object), not just that JSON.parse succeeded; null, numbers and arrays are valid JSON.

evidence: git() catches every error and returns null, yet its comment says null means 'git exited non-zero ... an absent value, not a masked error'. That comment is false for spawn failures such as ENOENT on the git binary. On this thread the agent gave no reply; it had declined the identical round-2 finding in an issue comment. Graceful degradation is a defensible product choice, but the agent had applied no-silent-failure to the stash count in round 0 and then exempted the spawn error, and the code comment misrepresents what is caught.
guidance_note: When a catch-all is meant to model one specific absence (non-zero exit), discriminate it in the catch (e.status vs e.code) or make the comment state what is actually swallowed.

narrative: This was a small standalone script reviewed four times. Rounds 0-2 put every finding in the summary body ('outside the reviewed diff'), and the agent answered them in issue comments, fixing most. Round 1 re-raised malformed stdin because the round-0 fix took the 'thread one cwd' option instead of 'fail loudly'. Round 1 also carried new findings on original code, so that round would have run anyway. The PR merged with both round-3 inline threads unanswered, one of them a real crash on a valid JSON `null` payload.
guidance_observations: Merging with an unanswered inline finding that names a concrete crash skips the review loop the process requires.
Answering review-body findings in an issue comment leaves no per-finding thread, so the later repeat of a declined finding (git spawn errors) arrived with no visible prior decision.

evidence: globals.palette and variables.theme.default both hold "catppuccin-mocha", and the comment over them claimed [LAW:one-source-of-truth]. Two literals that must agree are two sources. The agent conceded this in F5 ('my first pushback leaned on "it is the accepted idiom", which does not answer the law'), and #145 then implemented the runtime single source. no-mode-explosion was applied to the reviewer's suggested loader rule, not to the drift itself.
guidance_note: Before citing a law in a code comment, check that the code satisfies it; a comment claiming one-source-of-truth over two hand-synced literals invites exactly this finding.

evidence: The original payload had no git, home or cost data, so the gated git and directoryFull template branches never evaluated. 4797132 adds a rich daemon-shaped payload and content assertions ('◷ 13m', '~/c/c/src', '◆ 8'), so those branches now run.
guidance_note: When a test claims to validate templates, feed it data that makes every gated branch render; a test that only covers the gated-off path checks nothing about the branches.

evidence: The test hardcoded DEFAULT_WRAP etc. while legacy-parity sets autoWrap:false, so it did not render the config as the daemon does. Flag false positive: the hardcoded DEFAULT_* options were in the original test and 4797132 only moved them into renderExample(). The cited law is not served by the fix, which writes a third copy of the daemon's `globals.x ?? DEFAULT_X` resolution instead of calling a shared resolver.
guidance_note: When a test claims 'the full production pipeline', call the production option resolver instead of restating its constants.

evidence: The visible() helper with an ST-only OSC-8 regex was new code in 4797132, the F2 fix. The agent notes rich-js currently emits ST, so no assertion was failing; this is robustness, and the one-regex change is cheap.
guidance_note: When writing an escape-sequence stripper, encode the spec's full grammar (both OSC terminators), not the one form the current renderer emits.

evidence: This re-raises F1, which was pushed back without a fix, so caused_by is null. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive because 8d23844 changed only the test file. 52d8e2b rewrote the comment to call the pin a duplication, and the agent filed follow-up brandon-config-b9j, which #145 delivered.
guidance_note: Answer the law a finding cites on the first pass; pushing back with 'it's the accepted idiom' just schedules a re-raise.

evidence: The reviewer itself says the comment 'honestly frames this as a known caveat'. The duplication cannot be removed in a pure-data JSON5 file and is tracked as brandon-config-b9j. Flag false positive: 52d8e2b changed comments only, and the duplicated literals predate it.

narrative: The F2 fix (rich payload plus a new visible() helper) drew F4, a gap in the newly written regex. F3 flagged hardcoding that was only relocated. The theme-name duplication went round 0 (pushed back as 'accepted idiom'), round 2 (conceded, comment made honest, follow-up filed), round 3 (reviewer re-notes the documented caveat). Answering F1 the way F5 was answered would have removed rounds 2 and 3.
guidance_observations: The original comment claimed [LAW:one-source-of-truth] over two hand-synced literals; checking law claims in your own comments before pushing would have avoided two rounds.
Filing the follow-up ticket (b9j) instead of forcing machinery into an example file was the right scope call, and #145 delivered it.

evidence: The new field was typed `readonly theme?: { readonly effective: string }` right under a comment saying 'Always present', and buildRenderPayload sets it on every path. 7c5e20e drops the `?` and typechecks with no other callsite touched.
guidance_note: When writing a doc comment that asserts an invariant ('always present'), make the type say it in the same edit.

narrative: This was the follow-up that removed #144's duplicated theme literal by surfacing the daemon-resolved theme as `theme.effective`. One advisory: the type marked the field optional while the comment and the code made it always present. It was fixed in one commit, and round 1 was clean.

evidence: The PR made the lease load-bearing, but ensureSocketParentSafe lstat'ed only the socket path. 1bfed00 loops the symlink gate over [sockPath, leasePathFor(sockPath)] and adds a test, so one enforcer certifies both paths.
guidance_note: When promoting a file from diagnostic to authoritative, extend every safety gate that already guards its sibling resources to it.

evidence: Node's process.exit() terminates synchronously, so the described fall-through to unlinkSync cannot happen. The agent says it confirmed this: an incumbent socket was left untouched. It rejected the diagnosis but added the `return;` to match the sibling `retried` branch. That split answer is right.

`readLease(leasePath())` was original code, but the F1 fix (1bfed00) introduced leasePathFor(sockPath) with a comment saying it certifies 'the exact path it was handed, not a re-derived one'. It then left handleAddressInUse re-deriving from the global two lines from where sockPath is used. The values coincide today, so the premise overstates the risk.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a 'derive from the threaded parameter' helper, grep every call site of the old global accessor and convert or justify each one in the same commit.

evidence: The read-then-unlink TOCTOU in removeLeaseIfOwned is real but sub-microsecond, and #147's self-check heals it, so not changing the behavior was right. But the accepted residual was recorded only in the thread. In round 3 (F11) the reviewer re-raised it and explicitly offered 'add a comment acknowledging it', which the agent declined again. For F7 the agent did write the residual into the code. Flag false positive: removeLeaseIfOwned is unchanged since the original commit.
guidance_note: When accepting a residual race, write it into the code comment at the site, as was done for F7's pid-reuse case, so later review rounds don't re-raise it.

evidence: The original writeLease's writeFileSync truncates before writing, so a concurrent arbitration could read an empty lease, classify it 'unreadable', and reclaim a live socket. 42ff5a7 switches to temp-then-rename. Flag false positive: writeLease was original code.
guidance_note: When a file becomes a cross-process authority that others read concurrently, publish it atomically (temp + rename) from the first version.

evidence: This is the same finding as F3 in the same round, and the agent resolved both with one change in 42ff5a7. The gap is the call site that the leasePathFor helper added in 1bfed00 did not reach.

The agent conceded the pid-reuse wedge is real and a regression against the connect probe. It declined a behavior change and showed connect() would reopen the ECONNREFUSED storm the PR fixes, while a fingerprint is the deferred lock work. It then rewrote arbitrateSocket's failure-direction comment in 42ff5a7 to state the wedge honestly. Flag false positive: the arbitration logic is original.
guidance_note: When writing a 'failure directions' comment, state each direction's worst case, not its typical case; 'only makes us not start this tick' understated a permanent wedge.

evidence: 42ff5a7 threaded sockPath into the lease read only, and the comment there says 'one identity source for the whole arbitration', while writeLeaseFile kept calling leasePath(). fe845af threads it into the write too. The values coincide at runtime.
guidance_note: When threading a parameter to replace a global derivation, convert the reader and the writer of the same artifact together.

evidence: This duplicates F8 in the same round. The comment added in 42ff5a7 warns against exactly the re-derivation that writeLeaseFile still did, and fe845af fixed both threads.
The new lease-symlink test from the F1 fix (1bfed00) hardcoded `${sock}.lease` in the same commit that introduced leasePathFor as the single derivation. 6af4e34 imports leasePathFor instead.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces the canonical helper for a derivation, have that fix's own test call it instead of restating the formula.

evidence: This re-raises F4. The reviewer's option (b), 'accept the window ... and add a comment acknowledging it', was the cheap right answer, and the agent took that route for F7. Declining a second time leaves the residual undocumented in code. Flag false positive: fe845af changed only server.ts lease-write threading.
guidance_note: A residual risk accepted in a review thread belongs in a code comment at the site; the thread disappears after merge and the next reviewer re-derives the race.

evidence: Before review, every site used leasePath() consistently. The F3 and F8 fixes threaded sockPath into the read and the write but deliberately left shutdown on leasePath(), which created the two-form asymmetry this finding names. The agent is right that shutdown has no sockPath in scope and that stashing one in a module global is worse. The flag points at 6af4e34, a test-only commit; the real cause is the fe845af fix.
guidance_note: Before accepting a 'thread the parameter' finding, check whether every site can take the parameter; if one cannot, push back on all of them instead of producing a half-threaded mix.

evidence: The atomic-write fix (42ff5a7) added `try { fs.unlinkSync(tmp) } catch { /* temp may not exist */ }`, which swallows non-ENOENT failures and can leave per-pid .tmp files behind. d9693dc appends non-ENOENT cleanup errors to the returned reason.
guidance_note: When adding a cleanup catch in a fix, discriminate the one benign error code (ENOENT) and surface the rest, as the file's other catches already do.

evidence: `holder.pid!` in the original integration test would, if pid were undefined, produce a pid-less lease that reads 'unreadable' and makes the test pass via reclaim for the wrong reason. Unlikely after spawn, but the assertion is cheap. Flag false positive: the test predates 6af4e34.

narrative: Fix-caused churn drove most of the later rounds. The F1 fix introduced leasePathFor(sockPath) without sweeping existing leasePath() callers or its own test. That produced F3/F6 (the read), then F8/F9 (the write, missed by the F3 fix), then F10 (the test), then F12 (shutdown, deliberately left half-threaded). The F5 atomic-write fix added a silent catch (F13). The removeLeaseIfOwned TOCTOU was accepted as residual risk only in the thread and was re-raised in round 3. Rounds 2 and 3 exist only because of incomplete fixes; round 4 also carried a pre-existing test finding (F14).
guidance_observations: Introducing a canonical helper mid-review without grepping every caller of the accessor it supersedes cost three extra rounds of 'thread the parameter' findings.
Threading-only findings whose values provably coincide could have been pushed back once, as a set, instead of being implemented piecemeal into an asymmetric state.

evidence: No real-fs test exercised readSocketIdentity's non-ENOENT catch path, so dropping the ENOENT discriminator would have gone unnoticed. bedd49b stats a path under a regular file (deterministic ENOTDIR) and asserts 'unreadable'.
guidance_note: When a boundary function has an error discriminator, cover each discriminated branch with a real failure at the boundary, not only as input to the pure fold.

evidence: shutdown() always process.exit()s, the timer is unref()'d, and the displaced latch plus the idempotent shutdown make a stray fire a no-op. A module field holding the disarm handle would be state nothing reads; the agent notes limits' handle is captured only because describeNextRestart() is read.

The F1 fix's new test (bedd49b) used `expect(r.kind === "unreadable" && r.detail.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, which fails as `expect(false)` and hides the real mismatch. 57a04c0 narrows with an `if` instead. The reviewer also named the same pattern at line 109, and the reply addresses only the new one. This is about failure-message clarity, not behavior versus structure.
guidance_note: When adding a test in a fix, match the file's existing narrowing idiom (`if (r.kind === ...)`) instead of a short-circuit expression inside expect.

evidence: After displacement the interval kept firing statSync during shutdown. It was harmless because of the latch and unref, but the watch had finished its job, and the sibling armBinaryWatch already clears its interval before shutting down. f3803b0 clears the timer in arm() and tests that reads stop. The cited law is about hidden ordering dependencies, not timer cleanup.
guidance_note: When writing a periodic watch whose job ends in one action, clear its own timer at that action, as the sibling armBinaryWatch already did.

evidence: The comment said 'if the path is already not-ours here', but the code only bailed when the path was absent or unreadable. The agent rejected the reviewer's fstat(fd) alternative because an AF_UNIX fd inode is in the socket namespace and not comparable to stat(path); that holds. It fixed the comment in e057826. The comment defect is representation, not temporal coupling.
guidance_note: When a comment describes a guard, write it against what the condition actually tests (absent/unreadable), not what the guard is meant to achieve (ownership).

evidence: This re-raises F2. The agent shows makeLimits has the identical discarded-disarm shape and that shutdown() disarms none of the three unref'd timers. It also points out that disarm is exercised in test/daemon-parent-watchdog.test.ts, so it is not dead API. Wiring disarm into shutdown for one timer would single it out; the self-disarm on displacement already landed in f3803b0.

narrative: This was a clean module, with one finding per round, all advisory. The only fix-caused finding is F3, a short-circuit assertion in the test that the F1 fix added. The discarded-disarm concern was raised twice (F2, F6), and both pushbacks are well-argued against sibling parity. F5 caught a comment that overstated what the bind-window guard checks.
guidance_observations: The agent's distinction between F4 (accepted: the watch should stop its own timer) and F2/F6 (declined: shutdown should not reach into one of three identical timers) was explicit and consistent, which made the re-raise cheap to answer.
